title: Standard cohomology and coefficient coherence of point realization
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For each finite coefficient field $E\subset\Omega$ write $R_E=\mathcal O_E$ and choose a uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use $D^b_c(s,R_E)$, the derived-complete integral category over the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its rationalization $D^b_c(s,E)$, and the common-stage category $D^b_c(s,\Omega)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Equip these with the standard t-structures [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]. Let $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Omega}$ be the specified point realization functors [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with target the derived categories of bounded finite-dimensional vector-space cohomology at finite or common stages. Thus $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}(C)=\Gamma(s,C)\otimes_{R_E}E$ on an integral representative and $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Omega}(E,C)=(E,\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}C)$. Use the usual cohomological t-structure on module complexes; at $\Omega$ its halves and cohomology are computed at a common finite stage.

These realization functors are exact and t-exact. For $\Lambda=E,\Omega$, every $C\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ and every integer $j$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\delta_{\Lambda,C,j}:\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(\mathcal H^j C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^j(\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}C),$$
induced by the canonical truncation maps. On $C=Q C_0$ at $E$, it identifies both sides with $\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^j C_0)\otimes_{R_E}E$ via the canonical comparison between localized integral and rational truncations. In particular a heart object is sent to a complex concentrated in degree zero.

For $E\subset L\subset\Omega$, let $\varphi_{L/E,C}:\operatorname{Fib}_{s,L}(C\otimes_E L)\cong\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}(C)\otimes_E L$ be the canonical point-section scalar comparison, induced by the sections-tensor and completion maps. The square formed by $\delta_{L,C\otimes_E L,j}$, $\delta_{E,C,j}\otimes_E L$, $\varphi_{L/E,\mathcal H^jC}$, and $H^j(\varphi_{L/E,C})$ commutes after the standard scalar/cohomology identifications. These squares have the identity normalization at $L=E$ and obey composition for $E\subset L\subset M$ under the tensor associators. Thus the realization/cohomology maps in the common-stage category are finite-stage maps compatible with every further extension.

proof.text: The scheme $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian of dimension zero (its only local ring is the field $k$), and $\ell$ is invertible because $\ell\ne p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]: its last two sentences identify the completed integral category in this item with the category used in [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure], and give closure under ambient standard truncations and cohomology. Thus that proposition supplies the bounded integral t-structure with its ambient truncation maps. Apply [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] to this same category: $Q$ is t-exact and its truncations are canonically the localizations of integral truncations. These are the halves of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]. No identification of a truncation with the inverse limit of levelwise truncations is needed, so the extra Tor-compatibility hypothesis of those propositions is not used.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, Proposition 6.8.11(3), Proposition 6.8.14; agent assembly of exact sections, localization, and canonical truncation comparisons (not a separate assertion in Bhatt-Scholze).

proof.text:
Write $G_EK=\Gamma(s,K)$ on integral complexes. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], $G_E$ is exact on sheaves and derived categories, commutes with shifts, and has $H^j(G_EK)=\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^jK)$. The termwise functor $q_E=-\otimes_{R_E}E$ is exact by [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization] (take $L=E$). Hence [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] gives the natural cycle/quotient identification
$$H^j(q_EG_EK)\cong\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^jK)\otimes_{R_E}E.$$
Termwise tensor commutes with shifts and mapping cones: in a cone the differential is the same matrix of the two differentials and the map, tensored with $E$. It therefore takes distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. The functor $q_EG_E$ kills uniformizer denominators by making them invertible, and its extension on a fraction $f/\pi_E^n$ is $\pi_E^{-n}q_EG_E(f)$. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], every rational distinguished triangle is isomorphic to a localized integral triangle, so this extension is exact. It is precisely $F_E=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; that definition supplies its bounded finite-dimensional target.

proof.text: If $C$ lies in either rational half, [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] writes it as isomorphic to $QK$ with $K$ in the corresponding integral half. Step 2 shows that $H^r(F_EQK)=0$ whenever $\mathcal H^rK=0$. Thus $F_EC$ lies in the same half. Applying this to shifted objects proves preservation of both halves at every integer cut. In particular $F_E$ is t-exact.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, Proposition 6.8.11(3), Proposition 6.8.14; agent assembly of exact sections, localization, and canonical truncation comparisons (not a separate assertion in Bhatt-Scholze).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to $F_E$, using Steps 1-3 and the bounded rational t-structure of [prop-constructible-truncations]. Compose its two comparisons at $j$ and the shift comparison to obtain
$$\delta_{E,C,j}:F_E\mathcal H^jC\xrightarrow{\sim}H^j(F_EC).$$
The counit and unit characterizations in the lemma show that these are induced by the canonical truncation maps, and natural in $C$. Apply the same lemma to the t-exact localization $Q$ of Step 1. Its composition assertion identifies the comparison for $F_EQ$ with the composite comparison for $Q$ and $F_E$. On the integral category $F_EQ=q_EG_E$; its cycle/quotient comparison in Step 2 commutes with the truncation inclusion and projection, since an exact functor preserves their kernels, images and quotient maps. Uniqueness in the lemma therefore identifies the composite with that cycle/quotient comparison. This proves the required identification of both sides for $C=QC_0$ with $\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^jC_0)\otimes_{R_E}E$. For a heart object, preservation of both halves says that all cohomology in degrees other than zero vanishes.

proof.text: For $E\subset L$ use the canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], namely the inverse of $\Gamma(s,\chi)\theta$, followed after rationalization by the chain isomorphism $\beta$ of [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization]. This gives exactly the specified $\varphi_{L/E}:F_LT^{\mathcal C}_{L/E}\cong T^{\mathcal V}_{L/E}F_E$, where $T^{\mathcal C}$ is constructible scalar extension and $T^{\mathcal V}=-\otimes_E L$ on vector-space complexes. Naturality for integral maps extends to fractions: both composites multiply the image of $f/\pi_E^n$ by the same scalar $\pi_E^{-n}\in L$. It is therefore natural on the rational stage. The map $\chi$ commutes with shifts by [lem-weil-point-completed-scalar-shift], and $\theta$ does so by [lem-weil-point-sections-tensor-shift]. The degreewise formula $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes ab$ for $\beta$ also commutes with shifts. Consequently this particular $\varphi$, including its inverse direction, commutes with the specified shifts.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, Proposition 6.8.11(3), Proposition 6.8.14; agent assembly of exact sections, localization, and canonical truncation comparisons (not a separate assertion in Bhatt-Scholze).

proof.text:
The functor $T^{\mathcal C}_{L/E}$ commutes with truncations and their maps by [prop-constructible-truncations], so it preserves both halves. The functor $T^{\mathcal V}_{L/E}$ is exact by [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization], and the cycle/quotient comparison of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] gives $H^j(V\otimes_E L)\cong H^j(V)\otimes_E L$; it too preserves both halves. Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to the exact t-exact functors $A=F_LT^{\mathcal C}_{L/E}$, $B=T^{\mathcal V}_{L/E}F_E$, and $\eta=\varphi_{L/E}:A\Rightarrow B$. For each sign its natural-transformation assertion is
$$\alpha_{B,\tau,C}\circ\varphi_{\tau C}=\tau(\varphi_C)\circ\alpha_{A,\tau,C},$$
where $\alpha_{A,\tau,C}:A(\tau C)\to\tau(AC)$ is the comparison at $C$ for the indicated truncation (and likewise for $B$). Compose the equations for $\tau^{\le j}$ and $\tau^{\ge j}$ and then shift by $[j]$. Step 5 permits moving $\varphi$ through that shift. By the composition assertion of the lemma the resulting equation is precisely
$$H^j(\varphi_C)\circ\delta_{L,T^{\mathcal C}C,j}=(\delta_{E,C,j}\otimes_E L)\circ\varphi_{\mathcal H^jC},$$
after the canonical source-scalar/cohomology and vector-scalar/cohomology identifications. This is the asserted square with the specified maps.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], $\varphi_{E/E}$ is the identity and for $E\subset L\subset M$ its composite is $\varphi_{M/E}$ after the two tensor associators. The rational tensor maps retain these identities by [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization]. Pasting the square of Step 6 for $L/E$ with its scalar-extended square for $M/L$ gives top edge $\delta_{M,C\otimes_E M,j}$, bottom edge $\delta_{E,C,j}\otimes_E M$, and side edges $\varphi_{M/E}$ and $H^j(\varphi_{M/E})$: use the tower equation for $\varphi$ and apply the functor $H^j$ to that equation. The associators commute with cohomology because they are the termwise tensor associators; the composition part of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] identifies their truncation comparisons. This proves identity normalization and composition of the squares, including repeated fields.

proof.text: Use the pair-category descriptions of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. The functor $F_\Omega$ acts as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], using Step 5's $\varphi$ to conjugate the image of a common-stage arrow. A source distinguished triangle is isomorphic to one from some finite stage $L$. Its image is isomorphic, via those same $\varphi$ at the vertices and their shift compatibility on the last arrow, to $F_L$ of that triangle. Step 2 makes the latter distinguished. Thus $F_\Omega$ is exact. Each half is the isomorphism closure of finite-stage halves, so Step 3 gives t-exactness. By [prop-constructible-truncations], cohomology and its canonical truncation maps can be computed at a common finite stage. Represent $\delta_{\Omega,(E,C),j}$ there by $\delta_{E,C,j}$. Step 6 identifies this representative with its image after every coefficient extension, and Step 7 gives the required successive-extension agreement. For any arrow represented over $L$, naturality reduces to the naturality of $\delta_{L,-,j}$ and that square; hence the maps descend to natural isomorphisms in the Hom colimits. Their finite-stage inverses descend by the same equations. They are the canonical truncation-induced maps since their representatives are, and a common-stage heart object is sent to degree-zero cohomology.
